before: The founders' tile showed as a rim behind the business through "technology alone", then slid out up-left on "right partner behind it"; the business shrank and dropped off the bottom edge.
after: The founders hide fully behind the business through "technology alone"; on "right partner" they rise straight up behind it, faces above its top edge; both lift 140 px, higher than in the hook.
why: The climax said "steps out in front" while the voice said "behind"; the arc in → beside → behind has to land at the end (story, legibility, brand reviews).

before: On "alone." the business stood in colour on the tool floor: the same picture as the hook's "grow".
after: On "alone" it turns grey and sinks into the treadmill; the colour comes back only when the partner rises behind it.
why: Cause and effect visible in one glance: technology alone = held back; the partner behind = colour and lift.

before: The returning "grow" was an 84 px word far from the pair.
after: "grow" returns at the hook's 190 px beside the lifted pair, then scales into its slot in "We grow with you.", underlined in cyan.
why: The callback must be as strong as the setup.

before: "Finding the right solutions": one tool parked inside the cyan selector (the reel slowed on "solutions").
after: A full column of tools runs up at a constant 260 px/s through a selector that never settles.
why: A parked tile in a frame reads as "found" — the opposite of the line.

before: "Where to start?": two tiles broke out, the selector hopped onto empty canvas, and a different tool popped into the wall.
after: Three tools land round the business, the selector hops tile to tile, and the same three tools step into the wall.
why: No object appears from nothing; the hesitation reads as hesitation, not as a glitch.

before: On "hold it back" two blank navy squares appeared over the business's feet.
after: Two real tool tiles lift out of the floor under its feet (the floor keeps their gaps), then turn their blank backs as they grip.
why: They read as placeholders; now they are visibly the tools, and the brand rule (tools are never the villain) holds.

before: K.B arrived as a 220 px tile among eleven 220 px tool tiles of nearly the same navy.
after: On "K.B" the wall fades to 35% so the K.B tile is the only full-strength tile.
why: On arrival it read as a twelfth tool.

before: "TECH PARTNER" was two lines of 60 px caps under a small tile, partly covered later by the business.
after: One line of Copperplate at 96 px, centred under the docked pair, gone before the next phrase.
why: Unreadable on a phone; it is the positioning line.

before: The process ran on a grid of rounded cards on the canvas (a bento look), K.B squeezed at the left edge.
after: The business opens to the full frame in nine parts with 9 px gaps; K.B steps out and its lens does the work; the solution logos are 60% of a part's height.
why: Tiles carried almost every frame; the variety budget asked for a different structure in the longest beat.

before: On "life" the tools flipped back while the colour arrived, opening white holes in the business.
after: The colour floods out of the three tools first, over a full copy of the business underneath; then the tools turn back, with nothing showing through.
why: "Bring them to life" must visibly come from the solutions; holes read as a glitch.

before: "CRM updates" ringed a part showing a person, then a tool replaced him.
after: The ring goes to a part with a printed chart; no person is replaced.

before: On "from strategy" the business was wiped to an empty dashed grid.
after: The plan keeps the business at 25% inside its dashed outline, filling to full as it rides to "implementation".
why: The business never disappears one second after coming to life.

before: The founders' photo cropped the left founder in half.
after: The photo is framed so all three faces stay inside the tile at every size.
why: The real people are the point of "by your side".

before: The end card's line ran to 54 px from the right edge; the button label was 36 px.
after: The line starts at x 930 with balanced margins; the button label is 48 px; the line builds only after "grow" has landed.
why: Balance, legibility on a phone, and two texts never overlap.

before: The draft moved 8.2% of the frame in a typical frame.
after: The footage and founders' photo drift slower and the conveyors run slower: 5.6% (target 5%).
why: Karl asked for 5%: above every earlier film, without going past his references' range (0.5–6.6%) into a busy film.

before: Lurches (the business sinking, the hover tiles stepping into the wall, the lift on "behind", the grip) started at full speed from rest.
after: Soft starts (B3) or MOVE for everything already on screen; ARRIVE only for arrivals from outside the frame.
why: The motion probe flagged them; Karl's K.B lesson: nothing lurches.
